job.theme: the life of a famous Indian scientist
job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

response.passage: Dr. Janaki Ammal was a pioneering Indian botanist born in 1897 in Thalassery, Kerala. She dedicated her life to the study of plants, specifically focusing on how to improve sugarcane yields. In 1935, she traveled to the John Innes Horticultural Institution in England to conduct advanced research. Her work was crucial because her cross-breeding techniques led to the development of sweeter sugarcane varieties that could thrive in Indian soil. By 1951, she returned to India at the request of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to reorganize the Botanical Survey of India. During her tenure, she traveled extensively across the country, documenting thousands of plant species. She often carried a small notebook to record her observations, noting that the diversity of flora in the Western Ghats was unmatched. She spent 15 years working tirelessly to document these species before retiring. Her legacy remains a cornerstone of Indian agricultural science, proving that careful observation is the key to scientific discovery. She passed away in 1984, leaving behind a vast collection of botanical records that researchers still study today.
response.summary: Dr. Janaki Ammal was a renowned Indian botanist who improved sugarcane varieties through cross-breeding. She also played a vital role in reorganizing the Botanical Survey of India under Prime Minister Nehru. Her extensive research and documentation of plant species continue to influence agricultural science today.
